qualifiers: any quantity: length, time, data, energy...

answers.name: Metre
answers.fact: Now defined by the speed of light.

answers.name: Kilogram
answers.fact: Defined by a physical metal cylinder until 2019.

answers.name: Second
answers.fact: Defined by the vibrations of a caesium atom.

answers.name: Litre
answers.fact: One litre of water weighs about a kilogram.

answers.name: Celsius
answers.fact: Named after Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius.

answers.name: Parsec
answers.fact: A unit of distance, not time, despite what Star Wars says.

answers.name: Stone
answers.fact: 14 pounds; still used for body weight in the UK.

answers.name: Pint
answers.fact: An imperial pint is about 568 ml.

answers.name: Gallon
answers.fact: The US and imperial gallons are different sizes.

answers.name: Tablespoon
answers.fact: 20 ml in Australia, 15 ml in most places.

answers.name: Ampere
answers.fact: The SI unit of electric current.

answers.name: Volt
answers.fact: Named after Alessandro Volta, who invented the battery.

answers.name: Watt
answers.fact: Named after steam engineer James Watt.

answers.name: Pascal
answers.fact: The unit of pressure, named after Blaise Pascal.

answers.name: Kilojoule
answers.fact: What Australian food labels use instead of calories.

answers.name: Decibel
answers.fact: Measures loudness on a logarithmic scale.

answers.name: Acre
answers.fact: Once the land a team of oxen could plough in a day.

answers.name: Light-year
answers.fact: A distance, not a time: about 9.5 trillion km.

answers.name: Fathom
answers.fact: Six feet, for measuring water depth.

answers.name: Furlong
answers.fact: An eighth of a mile, still used in horse racing.

answers.name: Candela
answers.fact: The SI unit of light intensity.

answers.name: Lumen
answers.fact: How bright a light bulb is.

answers.name: Horsepower
answers.fact: Coined by James Watt to sell his steam engines.

answers.name: Mach
answers.fact: Multiples of the speed of sound.

answers.name: Day
answers.fact: The time Earth takes to spin once (roughly).

answers.name: Bar
answers.fact: Roughly the air pressure at sea level.

answers.name: Atmosphere
answers.fact: Standard air pressure at sea level.

answers.name: Coulomb
answers.fact: The SI unit of electric charge.

answers.name: Farad
answers.fact: The unit of capacitance, after Michael Faraday.

answers.name: Tesla
answers.fact: The unit of magnetic field strength.

answers.name: Sievert
answers.fact: Measures radiation's effect on the body.

answers.name: Chain
answers.fact: 22 yards: the length of a cricket pitch.

answers.name: League
answers.fact: About three miles, as in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

answers.name: Bushel
answers.fact: A measure of dry goods like grain.

answers.name: Dram
answers.fact: A small measure of whisky, or a tiny weight.

answers.name: Grain
answers.fact: Once based on a single grain of barley.

answers.name: Barrel
answers.fact: Oil is priced per barrel of 159 litres.

answers.name: Torr
answers.fact: Named after Torricelli, inventor of the barometer.

answers.name: Barn
answers.fact: A unit of area in nuclear physics: 'as big as a barn'.

answers.name: Shake
answers.fact: Ten nanoseconds, from 'two shakes of a lamb's tail'.

answers.name: Jiffy
answers.fact: A real unit in physics and computing, of varying length.

answers.name: Firkin
answers.fact: A small cask, about nine gallons.

answers.name: Planck length
answers.fact: The smallest meaningful length in physics.

answers.name: Smoot
answers.fact: An MIT bridge measured in a student's height, 5 ft 7 in.
